svg.title: Two obligation hints that could name work already taken, or the wrong run for a held tree
svg.desc: Left panel: a run classified scoring is asked whether a review is in flight. The reflex's own recorded dispatch answers first, and is honoured whatever revision the run now carries, because the live review it names is still under way. A hand-launched review carries no such record and is recognised only by the head-keyed record path its reviewer was granted, so a review of an older revision does not read as a review of the current one. Either match suppresses the review-missing hint; neither lists it. Right panel: a retained registered worktree is asked whether a live run now occupies that path. Occupied, the promoted run's ledger record still names the tree but the collector will not take it, so no worktree-held hint is emitted; unoccupied, the promoted run is hinted with one reckon crew gc command.
svg.text: Two hints, two decisions that keep them from misdirecting a coordinator
Each hint is emitted only while the work it names is still the work to do.
review-missing — is a review already in flight?
run classified: scoring
1. the reflex's own recorded dispatch
honoured whatever revision the run now carries
the live review it names is the thing under way
no live review run holds a pointer
2. a hand-launched review, by its record path
keyed on the head the reviewer was granted: an older head does not match
the current head does, so a standing review of it is found
no match at either lookup
in flight
lists no review-missing hint
not in flight
lists review-missing, with its command
worktree-held — who occupies the retained path?
promoted run, tree still in git's registry
a live run's pointer names this worktree path
the collector sees it live-referenced and leaves it alone
so the tree belongs to the live run now
occupied
no worktree-held hint:
naming the promoted run
misdirects at a tree it cannot free
unoccupied
lists worktree-held:
reckon crew gc … --apply
for the promoted run
Both defects fail the same way: the printed remedy is one the fleet would refuse
A review already launched cannot be launched again — a second dispatch conflicts on the review-store path the first was granted.
A retained path a live run occupies cannot be collected — gc leaves it, so a hint naming the promoted run chases the wrong run.
A hint is worth printing only while the work it names is still the work to do; both cases measure that condition.
